title: Your Bank Only Has 3 Cents of Every Dollar You Own
description:
Right now your bank is holding about three cents of every dollar you think you own. Not three percent of the bank's money — three cents of yours.

The rest isn't in a vault. It isn't anywhere. It's a promise, typed into a screen.

You deposit $100. The bank keeps $3 and lends out $97. That $97 gets deposited somewhere else, and lent again. One deposit — and thirty different people now believe they own it. Every one of them is right, as long as nobody asks. That's why a healthy bank can die in a single afternoon: nothing was stolen, everyone just showed up on the same day.

The alternative already exists. Under a wadiah (safekeeping) deposit your money stays YOUR money — held, not lent — and money only multiplies when something real was actually built. A lender risks nothing. A partner shares both.

Part 14 of The Money Machine, Decoded.
